items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: I had Joe Welsh was playing drum. And he was the only... Him and, let's see, Cantrell, the only two drum players that really played drum by music. That's Joe Welsh and Cantrell.

ctx.x: Did you have a teacher when you took up any bass or anything or pick that up then?

Well, I did have a teacher, a white fella. He gave me a whole lot of ideas on the fingerboard of the instrument. That was a fella called Matil Fertranger. Matil Fertranger. He had a place of business right here at Cornel and Claiborne. He was crippled. And he played at the... at the Orphan Theater. And he gave it up. But he was a good musician. So he gave me the fingerboard. You know, I used to bum around these places, see. And he'd take my liking to me. So he just gave me that fingerboard of the bass and gave me…
Who else was in the band when you were there?

items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: I was lucky enough, with Joe Welsh and Mary Monero, giving me instructions, instructions of divisions, you see.

ctx.x: Joe Welch, drum player. Yeah, he played violin, too?

Yeah, he played violin and drum. Uh, he, he did, too. Well, he helped me out a whole lot. He, he, he had, uh, I and him was bumming together, you know. We used to get out on the weekend like that, and, and me and him was good, you know, and I got good in the family with, uh, his mom and his sister. He had a fine sister, you know. She took a liking to me, and I got right into the family with her. So he, that made him, he had, be interested in me, you know, and anything that I wanted to know in the line of music.…
Well, did you ever play any other jobs for churches, besides St. Catharines? Did they have many jobs?
